chapitres.competenceChapitre: The learner can use language to keep abreast of modern technology, manage difficulties with appliances, practice politeness on phone/internet, and cope with social media.

objectifsLesson.description: Recognize names of gadgets (smartphone, tablet, laptop, TV, fridge, washing machine).
Read brochures, captions, and simple presentations with illustrations of appliances.
Draw and label pictures of gadgets and appliances.
Read basic texts and dialogues for specific information on managing difficulties.
Use polite expressions on the phone/internet (could you, would you, please, hold on).
Ask for, obtain, and give information through role-plays about managing appliance problems.

lessons.titreLesson: Politeness on the Phone and Internet

objectifsLesson.description: Read short texts and conversations portraying polite expressions.
Use nouns as gerunds (e.g., 'using a phone', 'sending a message').
Complete and rearrange words and sentences that express politeness.
Read short descriptions, role-plays, and instructions about social media.
Express likes, dislikes, and problems related to social media.
Write short messages, chats, and tweets on coping with social media.
Exchange information through dialogues and presentations on gadgets.
Use reflexive pronouns (myself, yourself, himself, etc.).
Express future time using 'going to + verb'.

chapitres.competenceChapitre: The learner can use language to explore citizens of the nation and the world, including local customs, cultural practices, and famous African and world leaders.

objectifsLesson.description: Read fables, legends, folktales, and articles about local customs.
Listen to stories and descriptions about traditional practices (weddings, funerals, festivals).
Use pre-modifiers (common adjectives) to modify nouns.
Read songs, poems, and narratives about local culture (dances, food, language, attire).
Use quantifiers (some, any, no).
Complete and rearrange descriptive sentences about local culture.

lessons.titreLesson: People and Aspects of Other Cultures

objectifsLesson.description: Read stories, narratives, and biographies about people from other cultures.
Use time adverbials (now, then, later, sometimes, always, already).
Express thoughts, feelings, and preferences about other cultures.
Read speeches, articles, eulogies, and biographies of famous leaders.
Use the imperative forms (e.g., 'Learn about your history').
Describe and compare leaders using adjectives.
Ask for and obtain information about cultural practices.
Give and exchange information through conversations and presentations.
Write short paragraphs about a famous leader or cultural aspect.

chapitres.competenceChapitre: The learner can use language to create environmental awareness, dispose of garbage properly, recycle used items, and explore interests and hobbies in relation to health.

lessons.titreLesson: Keeping the Home, School, and Environment Clean

objectifsLesson.description: Read instructions and guidelines on cleaning the home and school.
Write short narratives and advice on cleaning the environment.
Use intensifiers (very, too, so, quite).
Read notices and newspaper articles about garbage disposal.
Use interrogative pronouns (who, what, which).
Fill out simple forms on disposing household garbage.
Read procedures and processes for recycling with pictures.
Use cause and effect connectors (as a result, therefore, consequently, so that).
Write short texts on recycling used items.
Read illustrated stories and discussions on leisure activities.
Use verbs expressing likes and dislikes (love, enjoy, like, hate).
Complete simple reports on recreational activities.
Listen to peers talk about preferred recreational activities.
Use simple past tense for hobbies and experiences.
Write short descriptions of hobbies in relation to health.

chapitres.competenceChapitre: The learner can use language to discuss different jobs, job availability, common tasks, and volunteering in a work environment.

objectifsLesson.description: Read advertisements and brochures to identify names of jobs.
Use adjectives in the correct order.
Write simple descriptive sentences about different jobs.

lessons.titreLesson: Describing Common Tasks Associated with Jobs

objectifsLesson.description: Read short texts and pamphlets with pictures illustrating tasks.
Use the present continuous tense.
Write simple expository sentences on tasks associated with jobs.
Read job postings and advertisements about availability.
Use the first conditional (if + present, future).
Complete paragraphs and forms on job availability.
Read reports on volunteering at different work environments.
Use conjunctions such as and, but, so, because.
Write short reports on volunteering experiences.
Listen to simple radio or television news reports on jobs.
Express opinions, preferences, and interests about jobs.
Role-play conversations about job possibilities and demand.

chapitres.competenceChapitre: The learner can use language to create interpersonal relationships, describe homes, habits, routines, and household chores.

objectifsLesson.description: Listen to dialogues and role-plays where people introduce themselves.
Use modals: can, may, must.
Complete simple questions and answers about interpersonal relationships.
Read short texts to identify rooms (living room, bedroom, kitchen, bathroom).
Use prepositions of place (in, at, on, under, beside, near).
Draw and label pictures of homes, furniture, and furnishings.
Read short basic forms and guides on planning household chores.
Use the simple past tense (affirmative, negative, question forms).
Fill out simple forms and schedules for daily chores.
Listen to instructions and songs on performing household chores.
Use basic phrasal verbs (look up, look for, look after, look down, look into).
Write short sentences on cleaning different rooms.
Read short simple texts (songs, poems, instructions) about daily habits.
Use adverbs of frequency (daily, always, sometimes, often, rarely, never).
Write paragraphs on daily routines and habits at home.
